message: Danda । or double danda ॥: end a Hindi sentence with an ASCII period attached to the last word (STYLE 18.3, Microsoft Hindi Style Guide 4.1.12).
Space before a period, comma, colon, semicolon, question mark or danda: attach the mark to the word before it (स्थिति: {name}, फ़ाइल लोड की गई.).
Devanagari or other non-ASCII digit: write the digits 0-9 (PD-OI-106, campaign D-15).
Indian lakh grouping: numbers keep the English grouping 1,234,567, never 12,34,567 (PD-OI-106, campaign D-15).
Three periods or a doubled ellipsis: write one … (U+2026) attached to the word before it (STYLE 1.2).
ASCII quote in a Hindi value: write “ ” (nested ‘ ’). Code such as /key="value" keeps its straight quotes.
Period before a closing quote: put the period after the quote (‘यहाँ क्लिक करें’.), as the Microsoft Hindi Style Guide 4.1.12 says.
A hyphen between spaces is not a dash: rewrite with a comma or parentheses (Microsoft 4.1.12), or keep the source en dash – or em dash —.

Devanagari glued to a {placeholder} (e.g. {file}में, {name}का): a placeholder takes no ending or postposition; put a class noun after it and write the postposition as a word ({file} फ़ाइल में) (STYLE 18.5).
The verb agrees with a {placeholder} whose gender and number are unknown: put a class noun between them and let the verb agree with it ({file} फ़ाइल हटाई गई) (STYLE 18.5).
Loanword without its nukta: write फ़ and ज़ for English f and z (फ़ाइल, फ़ॉन्ट, फ़ीचर, डिफ़ॉल्ट, ज़ूम, ब्राउज़र) as Chromium does (STYLE 18.4).
Nukta where Hindi writes none: क, ख, ग take no nukta (Microsoft 4.1.12; ख़ास and ख़बर excepted), and native फिर and फैलाव have none.
Precomposed nukta letter (U+0958-U+095F) is not NFC: store the base letter followed by the nukta U+093C (फ + ़).
Anusvara on a word-final ा, ए, ु or ू: write chandrabindu ँ (दिखाएँ, पंक्तियाँ, यहाँ), as the Microsoft Hindi Style Guide 2.1.1 and the Central Hindi Directorate standard do.
Half nasal before a consonant of its class: write the anusvara (कंप्यूटर, अंतर, संबंध, प्रारंभ) as Microsoft 2.1.1 does; हिन्दी, एम्बेड and टेम्प्लेट keep their spelling.
English plural -s on a loan noun: masculine loans do not change (2 फ़ीचर, 2 ट्रैक, 2 रिकॉर्ड, 2 लेबल) and feminine ones take -एँ (फ़ाइलें); सेटिंग्स is the one established form.
Not a Hindi UI term: legend is लेजेंड (किंवदंती means a myth), strand is स्ट्रैंड (not रज्जुक), and GC, CDS, BLAST, SVG, PNG, TSV, GenBank and LOSAT stay in Latin letters (STYLE 1.1, 18.1).

Not the glossary word: feature is फ़ीचर (not विशेषता or सुविधा), record रिकॉर्ड, accession accession, legend लेजेंड, session सत्र; Select is चुनें, Try again फिर से कोशिश करें, Change बदलें (Microsoft 2.1.1).
Older य spelling: write लिए, गए, गई, किए, दिए, हुए, चाहिए (Central Hindi Directorate standard; Microsoft 2.1.1).
Informal तुम / तू or an -ओ imperative: address the user with आप and write the polite imperative (करें, चुनें, देखें) (STYLE 18.2).
Letters of another script (Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, Bengali and other Indic scripts, Thai, CJK, kana, Hangul, full-width forms) in a Hindi value: a token leak; rewrite in Devanagari or Latin.
Latin letter or digit directly next to a Devanagari letter: put one space between them (GC मात्रा, 5 फ़ाइलें, BLAST तालिका).
Spacing around parentheses or %: one space before (, none inside the parentheses, and no space between a number and % (5 मील (8 किमी), 50%) (Microsoft 4.1.12).
ZWNJ or ZWJ in a Hindi value: write the plain conjunct (कंप्यूटर, not कंप्<ZWJ>यूटर); Standard Hindi needs neither (STYLE 18.4).
Leading, trailing or doubled space, or an invisible character (NBSP, ZWSP, WJ, BOM): use single ordinary spaces only.
